userStories.title: Prefer packageManager and retry frozen installs across lockfiles
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `resolveBotChecks` on a base with `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json` and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint` and `packageManager` `"npm@10.9.0"` (no `.nax`, no instruction files) returns `preRun` `[{ command: "npm ci", timeoutSeconds: 600 }]`.
[unit] In that case the lint gate's command is `npm run lint`.
[unit] In that case `checks.install` equals `{ lockfile: "package-lock.json", reason: "package-manager", fallbacks: [{ command: "bun install --frozen-lockfile", timeoutSeconds: 600 }] }`.

[unit] On a base with `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json` and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint` and no `packageManager`, `resolveBotChecks` returns `preRun` `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `install` `{ lockfile: "bun.lock", reason: "lockfile-order", fallbacks: [{ command: "npm ci", timeoutSeconds: 600 }] }`.

[unit] On a base with `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json` and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint` and `packageManager` `"pnpm@9.0.0"`, `checks.install.reason` is `lockfile-order` and `preRun` is the `bun.lock` install.

[unit] On a base with `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json` and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint` and `packageManager` `"yarn@4.1.0"`, `resolveBotChecks` returns `preRun` `[{ command: "npm ci", timeoutSeconds: 600 }]` with `install.reason` `lockfile-order`.
[unit] On a base with `bun.lock` and `bun.lockb` (no other lockfile) and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint`, `checks.install.fallbacks` is `[]`.

[unit] With a base `.nax/config.json` that sets `quality.commands` and `execution.preRun` `[{ command: "make deps", timeoutSeconds: 60 }]`, `resolveBotChecks` returns that `preRun` and no `install` field.

[unit] With a base `.nax/config.json` that sets `quality.commands` but no `execution.preRun`, `bun.lock` and `package-lock.json` present, and a `package.json` that does not parse, `resolveBotChecks` returns source `config`, `preRun` `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `install.fallbacks` `[{ command: "npm ci", timeoutSeconds: 600 }]`.
[unit] With that config tier, both lockfiles, and a `package.json` whose `packageManager` is `42`, `checks.install.reason` is `lockfile-order`.
[unit] With that config tier, both lockfiles and no `package.json` on the base, `checks.install.reason` is `lockfile-order`.

[unit] A detected-tier result (no `quality.commands`) with a base `.nax/config.json` that sets `execution.preRun` `[{ command: "make deps", timeoutSeconds: 60 }]`, `bun.lock` present and a `package.json` with `scripts.lint` has `preRun` `make deps` and no `install` field.
[unit] `runBotInstall` with `preRun` `[A]`, `install.fallbacks` `[B]`, and a `run` that rejects `PRE_RUN_FAILED` for `A` and resolves for `B`, resolves `{ ran: [B] }`.
[unit] In that case `run` was called with steps `[A]` and then `[B]`, both with the given workdir.
[unit] In that case a warning log line names the failed command `A` and the next command `B`.

[unit] `runBotInstall` with fallbacks `[B, C]` and a `run` that rejects `PRE_RUN_FAILED` for `A`, `B` and `C` rejects with a `NaxError` `PRE_RUN_FAILED` whose `context.command` is `A` and `context.tried` is the array of command strings `[A, B, C]`.
[unit] `runBotInstall` whose first `run` call rejects with an error whose code is not `PRE_RUN_FAILED` rejects with that same error and makes no further `run` call.
[unit] `runBotInstall` with no `install` field and a failing `preRun` rejects with the original `PRE_RUN_FAILED` error after exactly one `run` call.
[unit] `runBotInstall` whose `preRun` succeeds resolves `{ ran: preRun }` and calls `run` once.

[integration] `runBotReview` on a trusted PR whose resolved checks carry `preRun` `[A]` and `install.fallbacks` `[B]`, with `_botReviewDeps.runPreRunSteps` rejecting `PRE_RUN_FAILED` for `A` and resolving for `B`, posts a summary with no `Install step failed` line.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, the checkout state given to the review lists `B` as the setup command, not `A`.

[integration] `runBotFix` whose checks carry `preRun` `[A]` and `install.fallbacks` `[B]`, with `_botFixDeps.runPreRunSteps` rejecting `PRE_RUN_FAILED` for `A` and resolving for `B`, calls `runBranchFix` and does not end `setup-failed`.
[integration] In that `runBotFix`, the fix prompt's checkout state lists `B` as the setup command, not `A`.

[unit] A present lockfile's inspection or read failing, or the base `package.json`'s inspection or read failing (not the file being missing), fails the derivation as today: `resolveBotChecks` yields source `none` in the detected tier, and in the config tier keeps its gates with no derived install and emits the existing warning.

routing.reasoning: Introduces install-choice provenance and a bounded fallback abstraction across detection, review preparation and fix graph environments; requires command-level seam tests as well as leaf tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: "US-003 AC-1/2: bun scripts resolve detected ordered gates" asserts the whole `resolveBotChecks` result with `toEqual` on `{ source, gates, preRun }`; a lockfile-derived result now also carries `install`, so the expectation adds `install: { lockfile: "bun.lock", reason: "lockfile-order", fallbacks: [] }`. Gates and `preRun` stay as asserted.

the "US-003 %s: lockfile selects prefix and install" table asserts each whole result with `toEqual`; rows whose lockfile has an install (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb) now also expect `install: { lockfile: <that file>, reason: "lockfile-order", fallbacks: [] }`; the yarn.lock and no-lockfile rows expect no `install` field. Prefixes and `preRun` stay as asserted.

userStories.title: Refresh failed saved installs from the target tip and explain setup failures
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Retry a failed saved install once using a different install resolved from the current target tip, retaining saved gates and explaining the final failure's origin and override.

**Motivation** — A target-branch MR added `execution.preRun: npm ci`.

**Approach** — **US-002 — fix re-resolves a failed saved install.** Inside `initialFixState`, the checks count as saved when `env.review.version >= 2 && env.review.checks != null` (the same rule `fixChecks` uses). When `runBotInstall` throws `PRE_RUN_FAILED` and the checks are saved, the fix calls `resolveFixChecks(env)` (the same `_botFixDeps.resolveBotChecks` call `fixChecks` makes, with `repoRoot`, the checkout's `baseSha` (the target tip), `snapshotDir`, `hasBaseNax`, config and the same `extract` callback through the fix's own call context, so an instruction-tier extraction is billed to this run like the initial resolve). If the fresh `preRun` is non-empty and its commands differ from the saved ones, it logs `Saved install failed; retrying with the install resolved from the base tip` (component `bot-fix`) with both command lists and calls `runBotInstall` once with the saved checks' `preRun`/`install` replaced by the fresh ones. Success continues the fix with the saved gates and the fresh install; failure, an identical fresh install, or an empty fresh `preRun` ends `setup-failed`. `setupHint` (built in `bot/fix-setup.ts`; every lockfile name and command in it goes through `safeCode`, as the setup-failed sentence does) describes the checks whose install failed last (the fresh ones when a retry ran, else the saved ones): `The install step was derived from \`<lockfile>\` (<the packageManager field | the first lockfile found>) on the base branch.` when `install` is present, plus `Also tried: \`<command>\`, ...` when `context.tried` lists more than one command, then always `Set execution.preRun in the base branch's .nax/config.json to choose the install step; after it is merged, the next nax bot fix <n> re-reads it, or run nax bot review <n> to refresh the saved checks.` The in-place "checkout not clean after setup" outcome gets no `setupHint`.

**Integration** — `fixChecks` (`bot/fix-run.ts`). Target (US-002): its `resolveBotChecks` call (with `repoRoot`, `baseSha`, `snapshotDir`, `hasBaseNax`, `config` and the `botChecksExtractOp` `extract` callback) moves into `resolveFixChecks(env)` in the new `bot/fix-setup.ts`, which both `fixChecks` and the re-resolve call; the saved-checks short-circuit stays in `fixChecks`.
`BotFixState` (`bot/fix-steps.ts`). Baseline: `setupFailed?: string`. Target: gains `setupHint?: string`; `outcomeText` (`bot/fix-outcome-text.ts`) renders it on the line after the setup-failed sentence. `fix-run.ts` is 509 lines, so the hint builder and `resolveFixChecks` live in the new `bot/fix-setup.ts` (US-002).
`checksSchema` (`bot/fix-input.ts`). Baseline: `source`, `gates`, `preRun` (zod strips unknown keys, so an artifact carrying `install` already passes). Target (US-002): also validates an optional `install` of the `BotInstallChoice` shape; an artifact whose `install` is malformed is ignored like any other invalid checks.
`initialFixState` extends US-001's `{ state: BotFixState; checks: BotChecks }` return so the running fix prompt receives the fresh successful install, not the old failed one. Use `runBotInstall`'s returned `ran` steps after any fallback inside the retry. Keep build execution separate and unchanged.

**Scope** — In: new fix-setup.ts resolver/hint builder, saved-install re-resolution in initialFixState, outcomeText hint rendering and optional persisted install validation, plus unit/command-level tests. Out: US-001 manager selection/fallback mechanics; US-003/004 rebase detection and findings/coverage carry. Re-resolving the saved gates (not only the install) in `nax bot fix`; the gates stay as the head's review saved them (#3027 ruling, #2628 design). Changing the saved review artifact's checks after a fallback or re-resolved install succeeds; only the running command's checks change. Changing the `--in-place` cleanliness check: a fallback or re-resolved install that dirties an in-place checkout ends `setup-failed` with "in-place checkout not clean after setup", as any install does today. `nax bot fix` accepting a review of a different head; its exact-head rule is unchanged (#3028 ruling).

**Interface** — `resolveFixChecks(env)` uses the existing resolveBotChecks inputs and the fix's own `_workflowDeps.callOp(ctx.callCtx, botChecksExtractOp, { ...input, model: config.bot?.models.checks })` extraction callback. `BotFixState.setupHint?: string`; `initialFixState(env, outputDir, input)` returns `{ state: BotFixState; checks: BotChecks }`. Persisted `checks.install?: BotInstallChoice` validates `lockfile`, `reason: "package-manager" | "lockfile-order"` and readonly-compatible `fallbacks` of `PreRunStepConfig`. Read-only `PrCheckout.baseSha` is the fetched target-branch tip, not mergeBase. Re-resolve exceptions are logged and become setup-failed on the saved command; no retry for unsaved checks, an empty new preRun or identical command strings. Use the existing makeBotFixEnv version-1 fixture for unsaved regressions and explicit version-3 checks for retry scenarios. Scope includes the public fix summary and outcome line plus persisted-input validation tests; no new CLI flag or gate refresh is introduced. For AC2, the initial resolveBotChecks call is the one that produced the persisted head review's checks; the failed replay triggers the second resolution across that save-and-replay lifecycle. A runBotFix invocation starting with saved checks calls the resolver only for that re-resolve, preserving fixChecks' saved-checks short-circuit.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] `runBotFix` whose head review is `version: 3` with saved checks whose `preRun` is `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, where that install fails and `_botFixDeps.resolveBotChecks` returns `preRun` `npm ci` which succeeds, calls `runBranchFix` and does not end `setup-failed`.
[integration] In that case `_botFixDeps.resolveBotChecks` is called a second time (the re-resolve), with `baseSha` equal to the checkout's `baseSha` and `repoRoot` equal to the fix's repo root.
[integration] In that case the fix prompt's checkout state lists `npm ci` as the setup command, not `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.
[integration] In that case the gate commands the fix runs are the saved review's gates, not the re-resolved ones.
[integration] In that case an info log line with message `Saved install failed; retrying with the install resolved from the base tip` carries both command lists.
[integration] When the saved install fails and `resolveBotChecks` returns the identical `preRun`, `runBotFix` ends `setup-failed` naming the saved command, and `runPreRunSteps` was called once.
[integration] When the saved install fails and `resolveBotChecks` returns `preRun` `[]`, `runBotFix` ends `setup-failed` naming the saved command, and `runPreRunSteps` was called once.
[integration] When the saved install fails and the re-resolved install also fails, `runBotFix` ends `setup-failed` with `setupFailed` naming the re-resolved command.
[integration] When the saved install fails and `resolveBotChecks` rejects, `runBotFix` ends `setup-failed` naming the saved command and does not reject.
[integration] When the head review is `version: 1` (no saved checks) and the install fails, `runBotFix` ends `setup-failed` and `resolveBotChecks` was called exactly once (the initial resolve).

[unit] `outcomeText` for a `setup-failed` state with `setupFailed: "bun install --frozen-lockfile"` and a `setupHint` returns text whose first line is ``Setup failed at `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; nothing ran.``
[unit] For that state, the text's second line equals the `setupHint`.

[integration] The fix summary posted for a setup failure whose checks carry `install` `{ lockfile: "bun.lock", reason: "lockfile-order" }` contains ``derived from `bun.lock` (the first lockfile found) on the base branch``.
[integration] The fix summary posted for a setup failure whose checks carry `install` reason `package-manager` contains `(the packageManager field)`.
[integration] The fix summary posted for a setup failure whose error `context.tried` is `[A, B]` contains ``Also tried: `B` ``.
[integration] The fix summary posted for any install setup failure on PR 42 contains `Set execution.preRun in the base branch's .nax/config.json` and `nax bot review 42`.
[unit] `loadLatestReview` returns `null` when the head's only artifact has `checks.install.reason` `"other"`.
[unit] `loadLatestReview` returns the head's artifact when its `checks.install` is `{ lockfile: "bun.lock", reason: "lockfile-order", fallbacks: [] }`.
[unit] The `setupHint` built for an install whose `lockfile` is ``a`b.lock`` renders the name through `safeCode`, so the hint contains no unbalanced backtick.
[integration] When `resolveBotChecks` rejects during the re-resolve after a saved install failure, `runBotFix` logs the error.

routing.reasoning: Five production files use existing resolver/deps, NaxError and rendering patterns for a single bounded retry plus optional schema validation; standard unit and command-seam TDD is sufficient.

userStories.title: Detect patch-equivalent rebases and record a rebased review scope
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recognise an unchanged patch rebased onto a later base and use conversation-only model execution while recording scope rebased and its prior reviewed head.

**Motivation** — The review re-read the whole PR from the merge base: $1.55, against $0.27 for the earlier incremental review, for an unchanged patch.

**Approach** — **US-003 — patch-equivalent rebase detection.** `reviewRange` keeps every existing rule. In the branch that today returns the full range because `reviewedHead` is not an ancestor of `head` (the ancestry call answered no, not threw), it first checks: `patchEquivalent` was given, `reviewedBase` is an ancestor of `checkout.mergeBase`, and `patchEquivalent(worktree, { base: reviewedBase, head: reviewedHead }, { base: checkout.mergeBase, head })` resolves `true`. Then it returns `{ rangeBase: checkout.mergeBase, conversationOnly: true, rebasedFrom: reviewedHead }`. A `patchEquivalent` that rejects is logged and answers the full range. `makePatchEquivalent(run)` runs `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff -U0 <base> <head>` for each range through `run`; a non-zero exit (an object missing locally) answers `false`; otherwise it compares `patchIdentity` of the two outputs, and a `null` identity on either side answers `false`. `reviewScopeOf` returns `"rebased"` for a defined `rebasedFrom`. The review then runs as conversation-only for the model (no package, no code read), and `prepareReviewChecks` resolves checks and runs install and build exactly as for any trusted review.

**Integration** — `BotReviewScope` (`bot/review-rulings.ts`). Baseline: `"full" | "incremental" | "conversation-only"`. Target: adds `"rebased"`.
`reviewScopeOf(input)` (`bot/review-rulings.ts`). Target: input gains `rebasedFrom?: string`; a defined `rebasedFrom` returns `"rebased"` before any other rule.
`reviewRange(input, isAncestor)` (`bot/review-rulings.ts`). Target: `reviewRange(input, isAncestor, patchEquivalent?)`; returns `{ rangeBase, conversationOnly?, rebasedFrom? }` (US-003).
`_botReviewDeps` (`bot/review-deps.ts`). Target: gains `patchEquivalent: PatchEquivalent`, defaulting to the implementation in the new `bot/review-rebase.ts` (US-003).
`ReviewCarryInput` / `reviewCarry` (`bot/review-carry.ts`). Target: input gains `patchEquivalent?`, passed to `reviewRange`; `ReviewCarry.range` gains `rebasedFrom?`, which `reviewCarry` also passes to `earlierCarriedFindings`.
`PrReviewInput` (`bot/review-step.ts`), `PostReviewInput` and `BotReviewArtifact` (`bot/post.ts`), `ReviewSummaryInput` (`bot/render-comments.ts`). Target: each gains `rebasedFrom?: string`.
`scopeSuffix` (`bot/render-comments.ts`). Target: scope `"rebased"` renders ` (rebase of <rebasedFrom 7 chars>, code review carried)`.

New module `bot/review-rebase.ts` (US-003). `post.ts` (592 lines) and `review-run.ts` (585) sit near the 600-line source limit, so rebase logic lives here and those files only forward `rebasedFrom`; if a forward would still push one past 600 lines, extract existing code from it in the same story.

**Scope** — In: patch identity/equivalence module, injectable default, range/scope detection and field propagation to carry input, operation input, artifact and summary; hermetic helper default and real git-rebase integration tests. US-003 may add the optional earlierCarriedFindings input field so propagation typechecks, but its changed carry guards belong to US-004. Out: US-004 carry semantics, coverage/readiness pins and not-reviewed quality mapping; US-001/002 install selection/recovery. Fetching a reviewed head that is no longer present locally (force-pushed away and gc'd, or reviewed on another machine) to compare patches; that case gets a full review as today. Recording a durable patch identity in the workflow item index so a rebase can be recognised without the old head's objects. Reviewing only the commits whose content changed in a rebase that also edited the patch (`git range-diff`); a changed patch gets a full review.

**Interface** —
```ts
export interface PatchRange { readonly base: string; readonly head: string }
export type PatchEquivalent = (dir: string, a: PatchRange, b: PatchRange) => Promise<boolean>;
/** sha256 of a `git diff -U0` text after dropping `index ` lines and reducing each `@@ ... @@` header to `@@`; null for an empty diff. */
export function patchIdentity(diff: string): string | null;
/** Default `_botReviewDeps.patchEquivalent`: diffs both ranges through `run` and compares their identities. */
export function makePatchEquivalent(run: typeof botGit): PatchEquivalent;
```
Read-only seam: `_botReviewDeps.runGit` is `botGit(args, workdir, timeoutMs?, maxBytes?)`, with no stdin. `prepareReview` returns without writing a review package when `input.conversationOnly` is true. Preserve all existing ancestry and full-review fallback rules; missing old objects must not trigger a fetch. Add `patchEquivalent: async () => false` to `makeBotReviewDeps` so existing non-ancestor tests stay hermetic and full-range. --full bypasses detection, and a changed patch remains full. Run command-level seam tests at runBotReview, not only reviewRange tests.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `reviewRange` with an index whose `reviewedHead` is not an ancestor of `head`, `reviewedBase` an ancestor of `checkout.mergeBase`, and a `patchEquivalent` that resolves `true`, returns `{ rangeBase: checkout.mergeBase, conversationOnly: true, rebasedFrom: reviewedHead }`.
[unit] In that case `patchEquivalent` is called with the worktree, `{ base: reviewedBase, head: reviewedHead }` and `{ base: checkout.mergeBase, head }`.
[unit] The same inputs with `patchEquivalent` resolving `false` return `{ rangeBase: checkout.mergeBase }` with no `rebasedFrom`.
[unit] The same inputs with `reviewedBase` not an ancestor of `checkout.mergeBase` return the full range and never call `patchEquivalent`.
[unit] The same inputs with `patchEquivalent` rejecting return the full range and log a warning; `reviewRange` does not reject.
[unit] `reviewRange` called with two arguments for a non-ancestor head returns the full range.
[unit] `reviewRange` for a head that descends from `reviewedHead` returns the incremental range and never calls `patchEquivalent`.
[unit] `reviewScopeOf({ rangeBase, mergeBase, conversationOnly: true, rebasedFrom: "a".repeat(40) })` returns `"rebased"`.
[unit] `patchIdentity` returns the same value for two `-U0` diff texts that differ only in their `index ` lines and the line numbers of their `@@` headers.
[unit] `patchIdentity` returns different values for two diff texts whose added lines differ.
[unit] `patchIdentity("")` returns `null`.
[integration] `makePatchEquivalent(botGit)` on a temporary git repository returns `true` for a commit and its rebase onto a later base commit that changes a different file.
[integration] It returns `false` when the rebased commit's patch differs by one changed line.
[integration] It returns `false` when the first range names a commit not present in the repository, and does not reject.

[integration] `runBotReview` on a PR whose index `reviewedHead` is not an ancestor of the head, with `_botReviewDeps.patchEquivalent` stubbed `true`, writes a review artifact with `scope: "rebased"` and `rebasedFrom` equal to the index `reviewedHead`.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, the review operation receives `conversationOnly: true` and no review package is written.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, `runPreRunSteps` is called with the resolved checks' `preRun`.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, the posted summary's first line starts `Review of <head7> (rebase of <reviewedHead7>, code review carried):`.
[integration] `runBotReview` with `full: true` on the same PR never calls `patchEquivalent` and writes `scope: "full"`.
[unit] When the old reviewed head is missing locally and the ancestry check throws, `reviewRange` returns the full range through the existing ancestry-error catch.

routing.reasoning: Adds SHA-256 patch equivalence and ancestry-dependent review elision across several typed seams; strict isolation applies to the hashing/cryptography override and provenance-sensitive decision.

suggestedCriteria: Given either compared range has an empty diff, makePatchEquivalent resolves false.

modifiedFiles.reason: `makeBotReviewDeps` returns the deps the review tests install; it gains `patchEquivalent: async () => false`, so existing non-ancestor review tests stay hermetic (no real `git diff`) and keep their full-range answer. No assertion changes.

userStories.title: Carry rebase findings and coverage to the new head and permit exact-head fix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve a pure rebase's blocking findings and complete coverage claim at its new head while keeping quality not-reviewed and allowing exact-head bot fix.

**Motivation** — To move past (2), the branch was rebased onto the target and force-pushed.

**Approach** — **US-004 — what a rebased review carries and records.** `earlierCarriedFindings` reads `index.reviewedHead`'s record for scope `"rebased"` when `rebasedFrom === index.reviewedHead` (widen and absent rules as for incremental), so blocking summary-only findings carry to the new head's carried record; inline threads carry as they already do through `mergeEarlier`. The existing `recordsCodeReview`, `advanceAfterReview` and `loadLatestReview` rules already treat any scope but `"conversation-only"` as a code review, so the coverage record is written at the new head (with no unread files, because nothing was read and the reviewed head it rests on was complete), the index moves to the new head and merge base, and `nax bot fix` loads the rebased artifact as the head's code review; US-004 pins these with ACs. `reviewQuality` reports `"not-reviewed"` for `"rebased"`.

**Integration** — `earlierCarriedFindings` (`bot/carried-findings.ts`). Baseline: returns no carry when `rangeBase !== reviewedHead` and when `scope !== "incremental"`. Target: input gains `rebasedFrom?: string`; for scope `"rebased"` the range guard becomes `rebasedFrom !== reviewedHead` and the scope guard admits `"rebased"` as well as `"incremental"` (US-004).
`reviewQuality` (`bot/post.ts`). Baseline: `"not-reviewed"` only for `"conversation-only"`. Target: also for `"rebased"`.
`recordsCodeReview` (`bot/coverage-record.ts`) and `advanceAfterReview` (`bot/review-advance.ts`) exclude only `"conversation-only"`; `advanceAfterReview` also refuses when the review left a required file unread. The workflow publish (`workflow/item-threads-index.ts`) sets `reviewedHead` only for a run whose review ran with nothing unread. So an index `reviewedHead` always names a review that read every required file.
`loadLatestReview(outputDir, ref, headSha, { codeOnly? })` (`bot/fix-input.ts`): exact-head match; `codeOnly` skips only artifacts whose `scope` is `"conversation-only"`.
`workflowPrReadiness` coverage hold (`bot/workflow-ready.ts`): applies only when the `w-coverage` record's `headSha` equals the current head.

**Scope** — In: rebased carry guards, not-reviewed quality mapping and command-level regression pins for durable carried findings, coverage, index advance and fix readiness. Reuse existing record/post/readiness behavior rather than introducing alternate storage or weakening advance safeguards. Out: US-003 patch identity/detection/field propagation; US-001/002 install choice and recovery. `nax bot fix` accepting a review of a different head; its exact-head rule is unchanged (#3028 ruling). Re-anchoring inline findings whose lines moved in the rebase (the `line_code can't be blank` re-post failures); unchanged. Carrying the earlier review's `quality` verdict to a rebased review; it reports `not-reviewed`.

**Interface** — Add or consume `rebasedFrom?: string` on the earlierCarriedFindings input from US-003, with `scope: BotReviewScope` including `"rebased"`; retain the existing CarriedRead shape `{ findings: readonly CarriedFinding[]; widen: boolean }`. `reviewQuality("rebased", "good")` returns `"not-reviewed"`. A pending carry-widen comment or unparseable old-head carry widens back to full review; a mismatched rebasedFrom carries nothing without widening, and absent records keep incremental's existing absence rules. Exercise runBotReview and runBotFix with stubbed rebase detection, real post/carry/artifact/readiness seams and shared fake forge/runtime helpers. Keep existing full, conversation-only and wrong-range incremental no-carry cases unchanged. PrReviewVerdict quality is currently typed as approved | changes (operations/bot-types.ts:33). Preserve AC5's literal runtime call with good, for example through Reflect.apply in the test, without widening that unrelated verdict enum; rebased scope overrides the quality argument. The existing carried-finding-holds integration file is near 800 lines; create the focused rebased-review-carry integration sibling listed in expectedFiles instead of overgrowing it.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `earlierCarriedFindings` with scope `"rebased"`, `rangeBase` equal to the merge base, `rebasedFrom` equal to `index.reviewedHead`, and a usable carried record for that head returns the record's findings with `widen: false`.
[unit] `earlierCarriedFindings` with scope `"rebased"`, `rebasedFrom` equal to `index.reviewedHead`, and an unparseable record for that head returns `widen: true`.
[unit] `earlierCarriedFindings` with scope `"rebased"`, `rebasedFrom` equal to `index.reviewedHead`, and a pending carry-widen comment returns `widen: true`.
[unit] `earlierCarriedFindings` with scope `"rebased"` and `rebasedFrom` different from `index.reviewedHead` returns no findings and `widen: false`.
[unit] `reviewQuality("rebased", "good")` returns `"not-reviewed"`.
[unit] `recordsCodeReview` returns `true` for a trusted workflow PR review with scope `"rebased"` (pin).
[unit] `loadLatestReview(outputDir, ref, head, { codeOnly: true })` returns an artifact for `head` whose `scope` is `"rebased"` (pin).
[integration] `runBotReview` of a rebased head whose reviewed head's carried record holds one blocking summary-only finding posts a carried record for the new head that holds that finding's key.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, the coverage record is written with `headSha` equal to the new head and no uncovered files.
[integration] In that `runBotReview`, `advanceReviewedHead` is called with `head` equal to the new head and `base` equal to the new merge base.
[integration] `runBotFix` on a head whose only review artifact has `scope: "rebased"` does not refuse and calls `runBranchFix`.
[integration] In that `runBotFix` with no push, the fix summary does not mark the PR ready while the carried blocking finding's key is in the new head's carried record.
[integration] With a pending carry-widen comment on the PR when rebase equivalence is detected, `runBotReview` widens to a full review using the existing carry-widen rule.
[integration] With an unparseable carried record for the reviewed head when rebase equivalence is detected, `runBotReview` widens to a full review using the existing unreadable-carry rule.

routing.reasoning: Production behavior changes only the existing carry guards and quality mapping; coverage, index advance and exact-head fix already admit rebased scope and need regression assertions, not new orchestration.

analysis:
Feature goal: close #3026, #3027 and #3028 without changing trusted-base execution, saved review gates or exact-head fix authorization. This is an enhancement of the existing Bun/TypeScript bot subsystem, entirely within packages/nax; no other workspace or dependency/version change is needed. Binding decomposition: exactly US-001 and US-003 independent, US-002 after US-001, US-004 after US-003. Graph-first navigation was unavailable because this host exposes no codebase-memory MCP tools; findings below come from direct source reads and text searches in the supplied execution root.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:145 documents the 600-line source hard limit, injectable external dependencies and small functions. Use Bun-native facilities and existing NaxError/logger conventions. Keep external work behind the existing command-owned deps; do not bypass runPreRunSteps or add direct shell/install execution. packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/pre-run-steps.ts:55 runs readonly steps sequentially, asserts trust, and throws an actual NaxError PRE_RUN_FAILED on failed commands; no-op empty steps and non-PRE_RUN_FAILED propagation must survive the wrapper. This work does not alter permission resolution, credentials or trust policy. Patch SHA-256 is a comparison identity, not authentication, but US-003 is assigned strict three-session-tdd because the specification's strategy override includes cryptography and this identity controls review elision.

US-001 discovery: packages/nax/src/bot/checks.ts:25 defines BotChecks without install metadata; :73 reads trusted base files through ls-tree/show and distinguishes absent files from failures; :93 selects configured preRun ahead of derived installation. The lockfile table at :180 currently orders bun.lock, bun.lockb, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock and :188 returns on the first present entry. Add manager metadata without changing order; inspect every entry, choose a present install-capable manager named by base packageManager, otherwise use the first present entry. Yarn has no frozen install entry; do not invent one. Deduplicate fallback commands, particularly bun.lock/bun.lockb, and retain 600-second derived timeouts. packages/nax/src/bot/checks.ts:209 builds detected script gates using the selected prefix; :229 applies independent lockfile-install fallback after the first trusted non-empty tier wins. Attach install only when the preRun actually comes from a lockfile, including instruction/config gates receiving a derived installation, never configured or extracted installations. Missing/invalid packageManager is not a read failure. Detected gates still require a parseable scripts manifest; invalid package.json can be ignored for install choice in the config tier without creating detected gates. Inspection of a later lockfile must not be skipped even after finding the preferred lockfile.

US-001 integration: packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:201 resolves checks then calls the review's runPreRunSteps; :255 runs build separately, :274 combines install/build setup reporting, and :353 renders checkout setup from checks.preRun. Return checks with the successful ran steps so the prompt and summary describe the actual fallback. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts:285 currently returns only BotFixState, performs installation, in-place cleanliness and optional build; :320 gives the original env to runStepGraph. Return { state, checks } and supply { ...env, checks } to the graph. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts:182 renders the fix checkout state's setup directly from env.checks.preRun, so passing the new checks is the essential seam rather than just changing logs. Build execution remains direct through each command's deps and keeps its existing warning semantics. Do not mutate/rewrite an earlier review's persisted checks.

US-002 discovery: packages/nax/src/bot/checkout.ts:175 fetches +refs/heads/<baseRef> and :197 resolves that fetched ref into baseSha; mergeBase is computed separately. The fix must re-resolve from checkout.baseSha, not mergeBase. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts:345 short-circuits to review.checks when version >= 2 and checks != null, otherwise resolves using repoRoot, baseSha, snapshotDir, hasBaseNax, config and the run's botChecksExtractOp call context. Extract that resolution into fix-setup.ts and reuse it after a saved installation's PRE_RUN_FAILED. Preserve saved gates/source, replace only preRun/install, and retry once only when the new non-empty ordered command list differs. Changing only timeout or metadata is not a different command list. Resolve failures are logged and reported with the saved command rather than escaping. Distinguish install failure from build warnings and from in-place dirtiness; only actual install setup failure receives setupHint. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts:50 owns BotFixState; :75 has setupFailed. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-outcome-text.ts:91 renders the existing setup-failed sentence with safeCode; add the hint on its following line without changing that first sentence. Escape every lockfile and attempted command using workflow/pr-body-safe safeCode; hint provenance belongs to the last installation attempted, not automatically the original checks.

Persistence/backward compatibility: packages/nax/src/bot/fix-input.ts:30 currently validates source/gates/preRun only and :54 ignores artifacts with invalid checks; :36 accepts versions 1/2/3. Add optional install validation in US-002 (as its explicit interfaces and ACs require), reusing positive finite timeout/command rules for fallbacks; existing artifacts lacking install remain usable. US-001 may persist install before this schema widening because the existing schema tolerates unknown keys and fixReview validates without replacing the original object. The failure table labels malformed-install handling US-001, but the binding explicit schema work and US-002 AC17/18 place this behavior in US-002; retain it there rather than moving those criteria. No artifact version bump, migration, historical rewrite or exact-head relaxation is required. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-run.ts:412 loads the exact head, :422 separately loads its code review, and :428 resolves saved checks. US-002 AC2's 'second time (the re-resolve)' is counted across the saved checks' lifecycle: the initial resolution produces the head review's saved checks, and the failed fix replay triggers their second resolution from the target tip. It is not two resolver invocations within a single fix starting from saved checks: fixChecks retains its short-circuit. A command-level fixture can persist the first resolution as the head review and then observe the subsequent _botFixDeps.resolveBotChecks invocation with repoRoot/baseSha and its own billed extraction context. No gratuitous initial resolution or saved-gate refresh is permitted.

US-003 discovery: packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts:185 defines the three existing scopes, :192 classifies conversation-only before incremental/full, and :203 validates 40-hex index SHAs, requires both ancestry relationships, and catches ancestry errors into full review. Preserve those rules and only check patch equivalence after a definite false reviewedHead->head ancestry result, with reviewedBase->mergeBase still true. An ancestry exception is not proof of a rebase. New review-rebase.ts normalizes only index lines and hunk coordinates and hashes the remainder; retain diff filenames, content, modes and other meaningful headers. Empty patches and unavailable objects never establish equivalence. Use botGit argv arrays with --no-color --no-ext-diff -U0 for both ranges, no stdin, no fetching old objects, no range-diff or model-based equivalence. packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts:58 is the existing bounded injectable git signature; :71 keeps hooks disabled. packages/nax/src/bot/review-deps.ts:34 owns isAncestor and runGit; add patchEquivalent there with the new implementation and pass it from runBotReview into reviewCarry.

Rebase propagation: packages/nax/src/bot/review-carry.ts:22 owns input, :36 range output, :46 picks full/narrowed range and widens when earlier carry is unusable. Extend the range's type to retain conversationOnly and rebasedFrom through scope classification, model input and carry decisions; --full must bypass all detection. packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:359 assembles reviewCarry input, :390 spreads range into review input, and :426 sets post scope/incrementalSince; forward rebasedFrom to post too. packages/nax/src/bot/review-step.ts:22 owns PrReviewInput and :130 returns early from prepareReview for conversationOnly, so rebase detection should reuse this path rather than write/read a review package. It may still run the cheap conversation operation; this is no paid code re-review, not a promise of zero model calls. Trusted checks/install/build are prepared independently before range selection at review-run.ts:509, so pure rebase must not skip them. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:79/:105 own artifact/post shapes; :359 persists artifact and :524 assembles renderReviewSummary. Forward rebasedFrom through both serialization and rendering. packages/nax/src/bot/render-comments.ts:349 builds scopeSuffix and :356 renders the summary heading; add the exact seven-character rebase suffix. post.ts currently has 592 lines and review-run.ts 585; place logic in the new module and extract existing code if field forwarding would breach 600. This concern is also shared with US-001/002 edits to these files, so re-read current files before implementation; the graph index cannot be assumed current.

US-004 discovery: packages/nax/src/bot/carried-findings.ts:143 currently rejects full and a range not equal to reviewedHead, then admits only incremental. Widen only the appropriate guards: rebased uses rebasedFrom == reviewedHead instead of rangeBase == reviewedHead, and admits scope rebased; maintain absent/unusable/pending-widen semantics. packages/nax/src/bot/carried-findings.ts:54 keeps blocking unthreaded findings by key and ends carry only on existing report/thread/settlement/provenance evidence. Inline threads already travel through post.ts:322 mergeEarlier. Do not re-anchor them. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:203 must return not-reviewed for rebased so summary, artifact and command result agree. packages/nax/src/bot/coverage-record.ts:68 excludes only staticMode and conversation-only and :82 writes the current head plus unreadFiles (default []); packages/nax/src/bot/review-advance.ts:45 refuses failed posting/unread/indexless review and :52 excludes only conversation-only, while holding advance for failed carry/coverage writes. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-input.ts:104 excludes only conversation-only for codeOnly, so rebased already loads as code. Pin these existing behaviors rather than replacing their guards with a new full/incremental allowlist. packages/nax/src/workflow/item-threads-index.ts:26 seeds provenance only for complete reviews, including refusal on reviewUnread; packages/nax/src/bot/workflow-ready.ts:24 applies coverage hold only to current-head coverage. Therefore carry the previous complete code review's coverage claim to a new-head empty-unread record and advance index to new head/merge base only after existing posting prerequisites succeed. Preserve carried blocking readiness hold when fix makes no push.

Tests and impact: packages/nax/test/unit/bot/checks.test.ts:65 owns the base files/input fixture, :106 configGates, :305 whole-result lockfile table, and :369 onward inspection/read failures. Add install expectations to lockfile-derived whole results, including the bun scripts result. Additional observed regression anchor beyond the spec's Modifies list: checks.test.ts:122 currently asserts package.json is never shown for config gates without an install; the new mandatory packageManager read requires updating that stale negative assertion while keeping base-only reads. packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-review.ts:8 supplies command-level fake deps and :54 stubs resolveBotChecks; add patchEquivalent: async () => false so existing non-ancestor integration tests do not execute git on fake directories. packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-fix.ts:6 creates a version-1 review at :52 and :72 supplies orchestration deps; saved-checks retry scenarios must explicitly use version 3 with checks. packages/nax/test/integration/bot/fix-setup-failed.test.ts:38 pins the unchanged sentence using toContain and :63 separates build warning/fatal failure behavior. packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-incremental.test.ts:117 pins ancestry/incremental/same-head and :134 full fallbacks; retain hermetic defaults. Also extend existing review-build.test.ts, review-checkout-state.test.ts, fix-run.test.ts, fix-input.test.ts, unit review-scope.test.ts, unit carried-findings.test.ts, coverage-record.test.ts and fix-summary.test.ts. packages/nax/test/integration/bot/carried-finding-holds.test.ts:1 is the existing two-head durability/readiness model, uses real postPrReview/loadLatestReview and fake forge; it is already 793 lines, near the 800-line test cap, so use a focused new integration sibling for rebased carry rather than appending a large scenario there. New test outputs are explicitly listed per story. Use actual runBotReview/runBotFix entry seams, not solely leaf wrapper tests, and a temporary git repo for real diff/rebase identity behavior. Snapshot/restore mutable deps and runtime/loggers using shared helpers. Tests are bun:test; targeted commands run from packages/nax with explicit paths and timeout, never bare bun test or bun run nax. Do not run coverage in NAX_SANDBOXED=1.

Refine audit: all 73 numbered spec criteria remain in their binding stories (US-001 AC1-23, US-002 AC1-19, US-003 AC1-19, US-004 AC1-12), with compound criteria split into observable assertions and existing-behavior pin qualifiers retained. All 19 failure-table rows are represented, including malformed install validation in US-002 per its explicit schema assignment. Every story retains negative-path and backward-compatibility assertions. All 13 feature-level exclusions are preserved verbatim; contextFiles match the five critical spec-recommended files per story, and binding dependencies/workdirs are unchanged. The retry count is clarified across saved-check creation and replay rather than contradicting fixChecks' short-circuit; detected preRun retains its array-of-steps shape; incremental-range tests require strict descendants; the conversationOnly seam is _botReviewDeps.runPrReview's PrReviewInput. US-002 is medium/tdd-simple because it changes five production modules through established patterns, and US-004 is medium/tdd-simple because its only new runtime behavior is carry guard and quality mapping while the remaining flows already admit rebased. US-001 and US-003 retain complex routing for their genuinely new fallback and equivalence integrations. The explicit spec call reviewQuality('rebased', 'good') remains an AC: operations/bot-types.ts:33 types normal quality as approved | changes, so test the literal good at the runtime boundary (e.g. Reflect.apply) rather than widening the verdict schema.

Risk/migration summary: optional metadata is backward compatible, but invalid present metadata must invalidate the artifact; provenance is base-owned, never PR-head supplied. Fallbacks must remain frozen and bounded, with no retries for arbitrary errors or configured/extracted installs. Report the successful command in both prompt environments without changing saved gates or durable artifacts. Failure after fallback must preserve first command plus ordered tried commands; failed fresh retry reports fresh provenance. Rebase equivalence is deliberately conservative: missing objects, backward/unrelated base ancestry, empty diffs, exceptions, changed patches and --full all retain full review. Do not equate model conversation-only execution with the artifact's conversation-only scope: rebased must remain a code-carry artifact for coverage and exact-head fix. Delivery is additive local modules plus command wiring, followed by carry/quality behavior; no CLI flags, new config schema keys, packages or release changes are introduced.
outOfScope: A non-frozen install (`bun install`, `npm install`) as any fallback: it rewrites a lockfile the fix session could commit (#3026 ruling).
Reading the package manager from AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md prose for the derived install; only `package.json` `packageManager` is read.
Changing the saved review artifact's checks after a fallback or re-resolved install succeeds; only the running command's checks change.
Install fallbacks for a configured `execution.preRun` or an install extracted from instruction files.

Changing the `--in-place` cleanliness check: a fallback or re-resolved install that dirties an in-place checkout ends `setup-failed` with "in-place checkout not clean after setup", as any install does today.
Re-resolving the saved gates (not only the install) in `nax bot fix`; the gates stay as the head's review saved them (#3027 ruling, #2628 design).
Recording the review's own install failure in the review artifact; `nax bot fix` detects a failing saved install by running it.
Fetching a reviewed head that is no longer present locally (force-pushed away and gc'd, or reviewed on another machine) to compare patches; that case gets a full review as today.
Recording a durable patch identity in the workflow item index so a rebase can be recognised without the old head's objects.
Reviewing only the commits whose content changed in a rebase that also edited the patch (`git range-diff`); a changed patch gets a full review.
`nax bot fix` accepting a review of a different head; its exact-head rule is unchanged (#3028 ruling).
Re-anchoring inline findings whose lines moved in the rebase (the `line_code can't be blank` re-post failures); unchanged.
Carrying the earlier review's `quality` verdict to a rebased review; it reports `not-reviewed`.
